To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have identified the most metal-pour damped Lyman alpha system to date, (2) we have used this system to constrain the mass of the supernova that produced the metals in this system, and (3) we find that this system is now suitable for low-mass star formation, but that this system may be related to ultrafaint dwarf spheroidal galaxies.

(a) we have discovered the most metal-pour DLA currently known, (b) the DLA is consistent with the nucleosynthesis of a 20 M_⊕ metal-free star that exploded as a core-collapse (Type II) supernova, and (c) this DLA has just crossed the threshold to form the first generation of low mass stars.
